title: [critic] prop:reductions case (a) is circular: cites 'contraction bound = content of (★)' to prove a case of (★)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** `solution.tex`, Proposition `prop:reductions`, case (a).

Case (a) handles the situation where one of $p,q$ has a repeated (but not all-equal) root, so the corresponding RHS term $1/\Phi_n(\cdot)=0$ and $(\star)$ reduces to $\Phi_n(r)\le\Phi_n(\text{other factor})$, the **contraction bound** $\Phi_n(p\boxplus_n q)\le\min\{\Phi_n(p),\Phi_n(q)\}$.

The proof then states this "is the content of $(\star)$ when one term vanishes." **This is circular**: the contraction bound is itself a nontrivial inequality (it is precisely the $1/\Phi_n(q)\to0$ degeneration of $(\star)$, i.e. a *special case* of the very theorem being proved), and it is nowhere established independently in the solution. Invoking $(\star)$ to prove a case of $(\star)$ is not a valid argument; case (a) is therefore unproved.

**What must be proved (independently).** The contraction bound $\Phi_n(p\boxplus_n q)\le\min\{\Phi_n(p),\Phi_n(q)\}$. I verified it numerically for $n=2..6$ (thousands of random real-rooted pairs, zero violations). A promising independent route: use the operator form $p\boxplus_n q=\sum_j b_j\tfrac{(n-j)!}{n!}p^{(j)}$, i.e. $r=Op$ for a hyperbolicity-preserving operator $O$ that factors into pieces $1-\varepsilon D$, and prove $\Phi_n$ is non-increasing under each $1-\varepsilon D$ (the Remark on $T_\varepsilon$ already shows $\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\big|_0\Phi_n^{-1}=0$ and $\frac{d^2}{d\varepsilon^2}\big|_0\Phi_n^{-1}\ge0$ locally; globalize this). Note the contraction bound is *weaker* than $(\star)$, so it is a sensible lemma to attack first and reuse.

This is distinct from q4-58 (circularity of the *vanishing-at-infinity* lemma in the heat-semigroup attempt); the present circularity is in the boundary-case reduction of the current MSS-based solution.tex.
